birth_prophet.title: Birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
birth_prophet.dateLabel: Around 570 CE (the Year of the Elephant)
birth_prophet.summary: Muhammad ﷺ is born in Makkah, in the Banu Hashim clan of Quraysh, around the year known as the Year of the Elephant.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Makkah was a religious and commercial centre of the Arabian Peninsula. Monday is mentioned as the day of his birth in a hadith reported by Muslim; the exact month and day are disputed.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The starting point of the Sirah.

birth_prophet.reliabilityNote: Distinguish the reliability of the hadith about Monday from the uncertainty about the month and day.

abdullah_death.title: Death of Abdullah, the Prophet's ﷺ father
abdullah_death.dateLabel: Before or shortly after the birth
abdullah_death.summary: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib dies in Yathrib, according to tradition on his way back from a trading trip; the Prophet ﷺ is an orphan of his father.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sources differ on the exact timing: before his son's birth according to the most widespread opinion, or shortly after.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: He grows up an orphan, which marks his early years.

halimah_nursing.title: Nursing among the Banu Sa'd
halimah_nursing.summary: Following the custom of Makkan families, the child is entrusted to a wet nurse of the Banu Sa'd, Halimah as-Sa'diyyah, and spends his first years in the desert.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: This practice allowed children to grow up in a healthy environment and absorb pure Arabic.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It sheds light on the social context of the Prophet's ﷺ childhood.

chest_opening.title: The purification of the heart
chest_opening.summary: An account reported in Sahih Muslim from Anas ibn Malik describes the purification of the child's heart by Jibril.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The episode takes place during his stay with the Banu Sa'd, according to tradition; Halimah, worried, then brings him back to his mother.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It is one of the accounts of the Prophet's ﷺ early childhood.

chest_opening.reliabilityNote: Account reported in Sahih Muslim; the exact date is not specified.

aminah_death.title: Death of Aminah, the Prophet's ﷺ mother
aminah_death.summary: Aminah dies while her son is still a child, according to tradition at Al-Abwa', on the way back from a trip to Yathrib.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The child, about six years old according to the accounts, is then taken in by his grandfather.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: He becomes an orphan of both parents.

guardianship.title: Guardianship of Abd al-Muttalib, then Abu Talib
guardianship.summary: Abd al-Muttalib takes in his grandson, then dies shortly after; Abu Talib, his paternal uncle, becomes his guardian.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Abu Talib raises the child in his family and will remain his protector for many years.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This guardianship explains the protection the Prophet ﷺ would later enjoy against Quraysh.

shepherd.title: The Prophet ﷺ as a shepherd
shepherd.summary: In his youth, Muhammad ﷺ tends flocks for people of Makkah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports that he did this work, as did other prophets before him according to the hadith.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the simplicity of his life before the mission.

syria_trip.title: Journey to Syria with Abu Talib
syria_trip.summary: Still an adolescent, Muhammad ﷺ accompanies Abu Talib on a trading caravan to Syria.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports a meeting with the monk Bahira on this occasion; the account is cited by biographers but its authenticity is debated.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This journey illustrates the importance of caravan trade in Makkah.

syria_trip.reliabilityNote: The Bahira account is reported in the biographical tradition; its reliability is debated by scholars.

hilf_fudul.title: The Pact of the Fudul (Hilf al-Fudul)
hilf_fudul.summary: Several Makkan clans conclude a pact to defend anyone wronged in the city. Muhammad ﷺ attends it in his youth.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports that he would later mention this pact with esteem.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the sense of justice that already characterised his conduct.

marriage_khadijah.title: Marriage to Khadijah
marriage_khadijah.summary: Muhammad ﷺ, known for his integrity, marries Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a Makkan businesswoman.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: He had led a trading caravan for her. Biographers report that his honesty had earned him the nickname “al-Amin”.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: Khadijah would be the first to support him at the time of the revelation.

kaaba_rebuild.title: Rebuilding of the Kaaba and the arbitration over the Black Stone
kaaba_rebuild.summary: Quraysh rebuilds the Kaaba. A dispute arises over which clan will set the Black Stone back; Muhammad ﷺ is chosen as arbiter.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: He proposes placing the stone on a cloak lifted together by the clan chiefs, then sets it in place himself.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The episode confirms the trust Quraysh placed in him before the revelation.

hira_retreat.title: Retreats in the Cave of Hira
hira_retreat.summary: Before the revelation, the Prophet ﷺ regularly withdraws for several nights to the Cave of Hira, on Jabal al-Nur.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: This account is reported in the hadith of Aisha on the beginning of the revelation (Sahih al-Bukhari).

content.heading: Significance
content.body: These retreats immediately precede the first revelation.

first_revelation.title: The first revelation
first_revelation.summary: In the Cave of Hira, the angel Jibril brings the Prophet ﷺ the first verses of Surah Al-'Alaq.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Most scholars place the beginning of the revelation in the month of Ramadan; the exact day is disputed. The detailed account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It is the starting point of the prophetic mission.

first_revelation.reliabilityNote: The account (hadith of Aisha) is distinct from the question of the date, which remains approximate.

waraqah_meeting.title: Meeting with Waraqa ibn Nawfal
waraqah_meeting.summary: Khadijah takes the Prophet ﷺ to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who knew the scriptures.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to Aisha's account, Waraqa confirms that what is happening resembles what was revealed to earlier prophets, and dies soon after.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This episode shows the first support the Prophet ﷺ received.

first_believers.title: The first believers
first_believers.summary: Khadijah, Ali, Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Bakr are among the first to believe in his message.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Abu Bakr then invites close acquaintances to Islam, among them well-known Companions, according to Ibn Ishaq.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: These first believers form the core of the nascent community.

first_believers.reliabilityNote: The exact order of the first conversions is debated among scholars.

first_prayers.title: The first prayers
first_prayers.summary: From the early days of the mission, the Prophet ﷺ and the first believers perform prayers, away from sight.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet ﷺ and Ali would go to the ravines of Makkah to pray.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They precede the obligation of the five daily prayers.

first_prayers.reliabilityNote: The precise form of prayer before the five daily prayers became obligatory is debated.

fatrah.title: The pause in revelation and Surah Al-Muddaththir
fatrah.summary: After the first verses, the revelation is interrupted, then resumes with the opening verses of Surah Al-Muddaththir.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: These verses command him to warn people and to prepare for the mission.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They mark the beginning of the call addressed to people.

secret_preaching.title: The discreet call
secret_preaching.summary: During a first phase, the Prophet ﷺ discreetly calls his relatives and friends to Islam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to Ibn Ishaq, this phase lasted about three years.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It allowed a first core of believers to form.

dar_arqam.title: The House of al-Arqam
dar_arqam.summary: The first Muslims gather in the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, near Safa, to learn and pray in shelter.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: It served as a meeting place during the discreet phase of the preaching.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the organisation of the nascent community.

warn_kin.title: The command to warn the close kin
warn_kin.summary: A verse commands the Prophet ﷺ to warn his closest relatives.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: He then gathers members of his clan to convey the message.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This episode opens the phase of the wider call.

safa_call.title: The call from Mount Safa
safa_call.summary: The Prophet ﷺ climbs Mount Safa and calls the people of Quraysh to listen to his message.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari, with the hostile reaction of Abu Lahab; Surah Al-Masad is linked to this episode in that narration.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It marks the beginning of the public preaching.

safa_call.reliabilityNote: The date of the public preaching is debated, independently of the soundness of the account.

quraysh_accusations.title: The accusations of Quraysh
quraysh_accusations.summary: Quraysh accuses the Prophet ﷺ of being a sorcerer, a poet or possessed, in order to discredit his message.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The Quran reports these accusations and answers them.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They illustrate the nature of the opposition he faced.

abu_talib_protection.title: The protection of Abu Talib
abu_talib_protection.summary: Facing pressure from Quraysh, Abu Talib continues to protect his nephew.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: He refuses to hand him over, although according to the reported accounts he did not embrace Islam.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This tribal protection was essential in Makkah.

weak_persecuted.title: Persecution of the vulnerable believers
weak_persecuted.summary: Believers without tribal protection, such as Bilal, Sumayyah and her family, suffer ill-treatment.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Abu Bakr frees several persecuted people, including Bilal ibn Rabah, according to tradition.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: These trials explain the first migrations.

quraysh_pressure.title: Quraysh's pressure on Abu Talib
quraysh_pressure.summary: Delegations of Quraysh ask Abu Talib to stop his nephew's preaching, then make him proposals.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to Ibn Ishaq, he refuses to give up his protection.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The episode illustrates Quraysh's growing opposition.

compromise_offer.title: Quraysh's compromise offer
compromise_offer.summary: Quraysh proposes an arrangement in which each side would worship the other's deities in turn; the Prophet ﷺ refuses.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Explanatory accounts link Surah Al-Kafirun to this episode.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It shows the firmness of the message on the oneness of God.

compromise_offer.reliabilityNote: The precise link between the surah and the episode rests on explanatory accounts of varying strength.

uqbah_abu_bakr.title: The assault by 'Uqbah and Abu Bakr's defence
uqbah_abu_bakr.summary: While the Prophet ﷺ prays near the Kaaba, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt chokes him with his cloak; Abu Bakr intervenes.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports that Abu Bakr said to him: “Would you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah?”

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The episode illustrates the violence endured and Abu Bakr's loyalty.

hamzah_islam.title: Conversion of Hamzah
hamzah_islam.summary: Hamzah, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, embraces Islam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Ibn Ishaq reports that he converted after learning of the mistreatment inflicted on the Prophet ﷺ.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: His support strengthens the community.

umar_islam.title: Conversion of Umar ibn al-Khattab
umar_islam.summary: Umar ibn al-Khattab, at first hostile, embraces Islam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Several versions of the account circulate in the sources, with varying degrees of reliability.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: His conversion strengthens the Muslims' position in Makkah.

umar_islam.reliabilityNote: The details of the conversion account vary according to the transmissions.

first_habasha.title: First migration to Abyssinia
first_habasha.dateLabel: Around 615 CE (5th year of the mission)
first_habasha.summary: A small group of Muslims leaves Makkah for Abyssinia to escape persecution.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Uthman ibn Affan and his wife Ruqayyah, the Prophet's ﷺ daughter, are part of it according to tradition.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The first migration in the history of Islam.

second_habasha.title: Second migration to Abyssinia
second_habasha.summary: A larger group of Muslims emigrates in turn, notably Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: They settle under the protection of the king of Abyssinia.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It shows the search for a safe refuge.

najashi_audience.title: The audience before the Negus
najashi_audience.summary: Quraysh sends emissaries to obtain the extradition of the emigrants. Ja'far answers before the Negus and recites verses of Surah Maryam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The Negus refuses to hand them over. This account is transmitted notably from Umm Salama.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It confirms the protection granted to the Muslims.

boycott.title: The boycott of the Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib
boycott.summary: Quraysh decides to boycott the clans that protect the Prophet ﷺ, who find themselves confined to Abu Talib's quarter.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to tradition, the boycott lasts about three years, then comes to an end.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the economic and social pressure endured.

year_sorrow.title: The Year of Sorrow
year_sorrow.summary: The Prophet ﷺ loses his uncle Abu Talib and his wife Khadijah within a short time of each other.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: This double bereavement deprives the Prophet ﷺ of two major supporters. The exact order and interval are debated.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: Quraysh's protection becomes more uncertain.

tribes_presentation.title: The message presented to the tribes
tribes_presentation.summary: During the pilgrimage seasons, the Prophet ﷺ presents his message to Arab tribes seeking support.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Most refuse, but these meetings prepare the ones with the people of Yathrib.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They lead to the pledges of Al-Aqabah.

taif_trip.title: The journey to Ta'if
taif_trip.summary: The Prophet ﷺ goes to Ta'if with Zayd ibn Harithah to seek support; the leaders of Thaqif reject him.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to tradition, he is driven out of the town. An account reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim mentions the angel of the mountains and the Prophet's ﷺ refusal to take revenge.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: An episode of patience and resilience.

mutim_protection.title: Return to Makkah under Mut'im's protection
mutim_protection.summary: On his return, the Prophet ﷺ enters Makkah under the protection of Mut'im ibn 'Adi.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The biographical tradition reports this tribal protection.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the importance of the protection system in Makkah.

isra_miraj.title: Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj
isra_miraj.summary: The night journey from the Sacred Mosque to Al-Aqsa Mosque, followed by the ascension.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The hadiths reported in the Sahih collections describe the main lines of the ascension and the obligation of the five prayers.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The event is central in the Islamic tradition.

isra_miraj.reliabilityNote: The reliability of the accounts is distinct from the dating, which is debated.

five_prayers.title: The obligation of the five prayers
five_prayers.summary: According to the accounts of the ascension reported in the Sahih collections, fifty prayers are first prescribed, then reduced to five.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account specifies that the five prayers carry the value of fifty.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They structure the daily worship of Muslims.

five_prayers.reliabilityNote: Authentic account reported; the dating of the event remains debated.

isra_reaction.title: The reaction of Quraysh
isra_reaction.summary: Quraysh reacts with disbelief to the announcement of the night journey.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition also reports Abu Bakr's confirmation.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the trial of faith in Makkah.

isra_reaction.reliabilityNote: Some details of the account are debated by scholars.

khazraj_meeting.title: Meeting with the Khazraj at Al-Aqabah
khazraj_meeting.summary: During the pilgrimage, the Prophet ﷺ meets a group from the Khazraj tribe of Yathrib at Al-Aqabah, near Mina.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to Ibn Ishaq, they embrace Islam and promise to spread the message.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The first link with Yathrib.

first_aqabah.title: The First Pledge of Al-Aqabah
first_aqabah.summary: Twelve men from Yathrib pledge themselves to the Prophet ﷺ.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The content of the pledge is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Ubadah ibn as-Samit.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It opens the way to a Muslim presence in Yathrib.

musab_madinah.title: The mission of Mus'ab ibn Umayr
musab_madinah.summary: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to Yathrib to teach the Quran and Islam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: He wins over many people there according to tradition.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: He prepares the welcome of the Muslims of Makkah.

second_aqabah.title: The Second Pledge of Al-Aqabah
second_aqabah.summary: Dozens of men and two women from Yathrib pledge to protect the Prophet ﷺ.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: According to tradition, twelve representatives are appointed.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It directly prepares the Hijrah.

companions_migrate.title: Migration of the Companions to Yathrib
companions_migrate.summary: After the second pledge, the Muslims leave Makkah in small groups for Yathrib.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The departure is discreet to avoid opposition from Quraysh.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The community re-forms in Yathrib.

dar_nadwa_plot.title: The plot at Dar an-Nadwa
dar_nadwa_plot.summary: Quraysh decides to act against the Prophet ﷺ by gathering representatives of each clan.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports that Ali sleeps in the Prophet's ﷺ bed that night.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This episode precipitates the Hijrah.

thawr_cave.title: The Cave of Thawr
thawr_cave.summary: The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hide for three nights in the Cave of Thawr before continuing their journey.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The Quran mentions the episode; Sahih al-Bukhari also reports details of the journey.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This episode illustrates the trust and friendship of the two Companions.

suraqah.title: The pursuit by Suraqah ibn Malik
suraqah.summary: On the road to Madinah, Suraqah ibn Malik pursues the Prophet ﷺ to obtain the reward promised by Quraysh.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports that his mount's legs sink into the ground; he gives up and turns back.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: This episode has remained famous in the account of the Hijrah.

quba_arrival.title: Arrival at Quba
quba_arrival.summary: The Prophet ﷺ stays at Quba, on the outskirts of Madinah, where the Quba Mosque is founded.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sources differ on the exact length of the stay.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The first mosque of the migrated community.

arrive_madinah.title: Arrival in Madinah
arrive_madinah.summary: The Prophet ﷺ enters Madinah and settles at the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports that his camel stops at the site of the future mosque. The year of the Hijrah is agreed upon; the precise day of the month is debated.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The beginning of the Madinah period and of the Hijri calendar.

masjid_nabawi.title: Construction of the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque
masjid_nabawi.summary: The Prophet ﷺ has his mosque built, on land acquired from two orphans.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It becomes the centre of community life.

muakhat.title: The brotherhood between Muhajirun and Ansar
muakhat.summary: The Prophet ﷺ pairs emigrants from Makkah with residents of Madinah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports the example of Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn ar-Rabi'.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It strengthens community solidarity.

madinah_charter.title: The Charter of Madinah (Sahifa)
madinah_charter.summary: A text organises relations between Muslims, tribes and communities in Madinah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: It is transmitted by Ibn Ishaq, but its form and date are debated.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It is important for understanding the initial political organisation.

madinah_charter.reliabilityNote: The transmission and form of the text are debated.

adhan.title: The institution of the adhan
adhan.summary: The call to prayer is instituted in Madinah; Bilal is the first muezzin.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Accounts of the precise circumstances vary according to the sources.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It structures the community's collective rhythm.

qibla_change.title: The change of qibla
qibla_change.summary: The direction of prayer changes from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The verses concerned appear in Surah Al-Baqarah. The exact month is debated.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: A key moment in the community's identity.

ramadan_fasting.title: The obligation of fasting in Ramadan
ramadan_fasting.summary: Fasting during the month of Ramadan is prescribed in Madinah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The verses concerned appear in Surah Al-Baqarah.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It becomes one of the pillars of practice.

badr.title: The Battle of Badr
badr.summary: The first major battle between the Muslims and Quraysh, near Badr.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports a little over three hundred Muslims facing about a thousand men of Quraysh.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It strengthens the Muslims' position in Madinah.

uhud.title: The Battle of Uhud
uhud.summary: A battle near Mount Uhud, marked by the loss of several Companions, including Hamzah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: It is mentioned in Surah Al-Imran.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It leaves lessons on discipline and trial.

khandaq.title: The Battle of the Trench (Al-Khandaq)
khandaq.summary: Madinah is besieged by a coalition; a trench is dug to defend the city.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Some historians place the event in 4 AH. Surah Al-Ahzab refers to it.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The episode strengthens the community's cohesion.

ridwan.title: The Pledge of Ridwan
ridwan.summary: At Hudaybiyyah, the Companions pledge themselves to the Prophet ﷺ under a tree, after the rumour of the death of Uthman, sent as an envoy.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The Quran mentions the approval granted to the believers who gave this pledge.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It precedes the conclusion of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

hudaybiyyah.title: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
hudaybiyyah.summary: An agreement is concluded with Quraysh near Makkah: the pilgrimage is postponed by one year.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: It is mentioned in Surah Al-Fath.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It opens a period of relative peace.

letters_rulers.title: The letters to rulers
letters_rulers.summary: The Prophet ﷺ sends letters to neighbouring rulers, including Heraclius, calling them to Islam.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports Heraclius's exchange with Abu Sufyan about this letter.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: They show the opening of the call beyond the peninsula.

letters_rulers.reliabilityNote: The exact text of some letters varies according to the sources.

khaybar.title: The expedition to Khaybar
khaybar.summary: An expedition against the oasis of Khaybar, north of Madinah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari reports that the inhabitants were kept on their lands in exchange for a share of the harvest.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It consolidates Madinah's position to the north.

mutah.title: The Battle of Mu'tah
mutah.summary: Three commanders appointed in succession, Zayd, Ja'far and then Abdullah ibn Rawahah, fall as martyrs; Khalid ibn al-Walid then takes command.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The first military encounter in the north of the peninsula.

fath_makkah.title: The conquest of Makkah
fath_makkah.summary: The Prophet ﷺ enters Makkah with his Companions; the Kaaba is purified.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Tradition reports a general pardon granted to the inhabitants.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It marks a major turning point of the Sirah.

hunayn.title: The Battle of Hunayn
hunayn.summary: After the conquest of Makkah, a coalition of tribes confronts the Muslims at Hunayn.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The Quran mentions an initial setback followed by the support granted to the believers.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It follows immediately after the conquest of Makkah.

tabuk.title: The expedition to Tabuk
tabuk.summary: The Prophet ﷺ leads a large expedition to the north in difficult conditions; the Muslims return without major confrontation.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: Sahih al-Bukhari also reports the account of Ka'b ibn Malik, who stayed behind with two other Companions.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It marks a test of sincerity and effort.

najashi_funeral.title: The funeral prayer for the Negus
najashi_funeral.summary: The Prophet ﷺ announces the death of the Negus and prays for him in absentia.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It recalls the ties formed with Abyssinia.

najashi_funeral.reliabilityNote: The account is sound; the date of the event is debated.

delegations.title: The Year of Delegations
delegations.summary: Many Arab tribes send delegations to Madinah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: This period follows the conquest of Makkah, according to the biographical tradition.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It illustrates the rapid spread of Islam across the peninsula.

farewell_hajj.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage
farewell_hajj.summary: The only pilgrimage the Prophet ﷺ performed after the Hijrah, with a great sermon at 'Arafah.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The account is reported in Sahih Muslim from Jabir ibn 'Abdillah.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: It sums up the essential teachings passed on to the community.

death_prophet.title: Death of the Prophet ﷺ
death_prophet.summary: The Prophet ﷺ dies in Madinah in the house of Aisha.

content.heading: Context and account
content.body: The year is agreed upon; the exact day of the month is debated. Abu Bakr is then chosen as caliph.

content.heading: Significance
content.body: The end of the Sirah and the beginning of the era of the caliphs.
